title: When Norwegian Uses No Article
goal: Use no article with common roles, languages, sports, mass nouns, transport, and indefinite plurals.

objectives.statement: Use no article with common roles, languages, sports, mass nouns, transport, and indefinite plurals.

spans.value: Amir has recently moved to Trondheim. His neighbor, Nora, has invited him to help at a language café on Saturday.
Hei, Amir! Kan du hjelpe på språkkafeen på lørdag?

blocks.translation: Hi, Amir! Can you help at the language café on Saturday?

spans.value: Ja, gjerne. Jeg jobber som lærer, så jeg liker å snakke med folk.

blocks.translation: Yes, gladly. I work as a teacher, so I like talking with people.

spans.value: Flott! Hvilke språk snakker du?

blocks.translation: Great! Which languages do you speak?

spans.value: Jeg snakker arabisk, engelsk og litt norsk.

blocks.translation: I speak Arabic, English, and a little Norwegian.

spans.value: Perfekt. Vi spiller også fotball i parken etterpå.

blocks.translation: Perfect. We also play football in the park afterwards.

spans.value: Det passer bra. Jeg spiller fotball, men jeg går ikke på ski.

blocks.translation: That suits me well. I play football, but I don’t ski.

spans.value: Det gjør ingenting. På kafeen har vi kaffe, te, brød og frukt.

blocks.translation: That doesn’t matter. At the café we have coffee, tea, bread, and fruit.

spans.value: Skal jeg ta med kopper?
Ja, takk. Vi trenger kopper og tallerkener. Hvordan kommer du dit?

blocks.translation: Yes, please. We need cups and plates. How are you getting there?

spans.value: Jeg kommer med buss.
Bra. Jeg kommer på sykkel hvis det ikke regner.

blocks.translation: Good. I’m coming by bicycle if it doesn’t rain.

spans.value: Amir and Nora are discussing work, languages, sports, food, transport, and things needed for an event. Norwegian often uses nouns in these situations without en, ei, or et. This absence is called the
zero article
: the noun has no article before it.
Notice the highlighted pattern in these phrases:
English sometimes uses an article where Norwegian normally does not, especially with occupations: I am
a
teacher, but Jeg er lærer.
When you say what role or occupation someone has, Norwegian commonly uses no article after være or after expressions such as jobbe som.

en.value: I want to become a journalist.

spans.value: The noun identifies the person’s role. It does not introduce one separate, countable person or thing.
Compare:

en.value: Sara is talking to a doctor.

spans.value: In the first sentence, lege names Sara’s occupation. In the second, en lege is another person whom Sara is talking to.
A compact rule:

statement.value: Use no article when a common role or occupation tells what someone is, becomes, or works as.

spans.value: A common mistake is to transfer the English article directly:
Not normally: Jeg er en lærer.
An article can appear when the noun phrase contains more description:
For this lesson, concentrate on the basic role pattern: Hun er lærer.
Names of languages normally have no article when you say which language someone speaks, understands, reads, writes, or learns.

A learner can also say Hun øver på norsken sin (She is practising her Norwegian), but there the noun has the definite suffix -en, so this is not a zero-article example. The central pattern is simpler:
Do not add et before a language name:
Not: De snakker et tysk.
Norwegian normally uses no article after spille when naming a sport or game.

en.value: He plays chess with the neighbor.

spans.value: The taught expressions gå på ski and trene karate also use the sport name without an article.

no.value: Nora går på ski om vinteren.

spans.value: Compare the activity with a physical object:
In the first sentence, fotball names the sport. In the second, en fotball is one ball.
The useful meaning question is:
Am I naming the sport, or one physical object?

sections.title: Mass nouns: food, drink, and other substances

spans.value: A
mass noun

names something treated as a substance or material rather than as separate countable units. Common examples include water, coffee, bread, rice, and cheese. Norwegian normally uses no article when the noun refers either to a substance generally or to an unspecified quantity of that substance rather than one countable serving or unit.

en.value: Amir is making rice for dinner.

spans.value: Compare an unspecified amount of a substance with one specified unit:
In everyday café language, en kaffe means one serving or cup of coffee. Kaffe without an article can mean coffee generally or an unspecified amount of coffee as a drink or substance.
Compare general and specific reference:
The first sentence refers to coffee generally. Earlier examples such as
Vi har kaffe og te

refer to unspecified quantities in a situation. The second sentence refers to particular coffee already known in the situation. This lesson teaches zero article for both generic substance reference and unspecified non-count quantities.
A compact rule:

statement.value: Use no article when food, drink, or material is presented as an unspecified substance rather than one countable item.

spans.value: Several common transport expressions use med plus a transport noun without an article. This lesson teaches med buss, med tog, med bil, and med fly. Bicycle travel normally uses på sykkel.

no.value: Hun drar til jobb med bil.

en.value: She goes to work by car.

spans.value: In the taught expressions with med, the noun names the mode of transport. It does not point to one particular bus, train, car, or plane. På sykkel is a separate fixed expression for bicycle travel.
Compare:

en.value: Amir is sitting on the bus.

spans.value: Med buss answers the question of how he travels. På bussen says where he is and refers to a particular bus.
Another contrast:
Do not copy the English structure word for word. Use med in the taught expressions med buss, med tog, med bil, and med fly, but use på in på sykkel.
You already know that a singular countable noun can use en, ei, or et:
When the noun is plural and means some unspecified people or things, Norwegian uses no article.
English may use some, but Norwegian often leaves the noun phrase without an equivalent word.
The noun must still have the correct plural form. Zero article does not mean that the noun stays singular.
Not: Vi trenger kopp when the meaning is more than one cup.
Compare the basic number contrast:
A compact rule:

statement.value: Use no article before an indefinite plural noun when you mean unspecified people or things.

spans.value: The same surface pattern—no article—serves several related purposes. In each case, the noun is not being introduced as one unspecified countable item.

basic role after er
Meaning:
language with a taught communication verb
Meaning:
sport in a taught activity expression
Meaning:

Meaning:

Meaning:

Do not use one mechanical test for every noun. Ask what the noun is doing in the sentence:

items.value: Does it name a person’s basic role after er or blir, or after jobber som?
Is it a language name used with one of the taught communication verbs, such as snakker, forstår, leser, skriver, or lærer?
Does it name a sport or game in one of the taught activity expressions, such as spiller fotball, spiller sjakk, går på ski, or trener karate?
Is it one of the taught transport expressions, such as med buss or på sykkel?

spans.value: If the noun matches one of these taught constructions and meanings, the approved pattern in this lesson uses no article.
On Saturday morning, Amir sends Nora a message.
Hei! Jeg kommer med buss og er der klokka ti. Jeg har med kopper og epler.

blocks.translation: Hi! I’m coming by bus and will be there at ten. I’m bringing cups and apples.

spans.value: Supert. Fatima er kokk, og hun tar med brød og ost.

blocks.translation: Great. Fatima is a cook, and she is bringing bread and cheese.

spans.value: Snakker hun norsk?
Ja, hun snakker norsk og fransk. Broren hennes kommer også. Han er student.

blocks.translation: Yes, she speaks Norwegian and French. Her brother is coming too. He is a student.

spans.value: Hva skal Fatima og broren hennes gjøre etterpå?

blocks.translation: What are Fatima and her brother going to do afterwards?

spans.value: Fatima skal spille fotball, men broren hennes skal spille sjakk.

blocks.translation: Fatima is going to play football, but her brother is going to play chess.

spans.value: The scene now contains all six patterns:

items.value: Hun snakker norsk og fransk. — languages
Hun tar med brød og ost. — mass nouns
Jeg kommer med buss. — taught transport expression
Jeg har med kopper og epler. — indefinite plurals

sections.title: Cumulative transfer: planning a study evening

spans.value: The situation now changes. A group of students is planning an evening at the library. They need to introduce the participants, mention the languages they use, plan a break activity, organize food and drink, explain how they will travel, and list the materials they need.

Without looking back, write one Norwegian sentence for each of these purposes: identify an occupation, name a language someone speaks, name a sport someone plays, mention an unspecified food or drink, say that someone travels med buss, med tog, med bil, med fly, or på sykkel, and mention several unspecified objects.
Then reread your six sentences. Check that target nouns have no article and that indefinite plural nouns use correct plural forms.
